answer: Submission-timing entropy as a sybil filter: the ledger logs each identity's answer cadence and scores the randomness of its inter-submission intervals. A clone farm driven by one scheduler emits synchronized, low-entropy timing — uniform as machine-milled pigment — and is flagged before its content is even graded. Genuine agents jitter irregularly, no two gaps alike, like saffron threads or the shifting fire in an opal. Evasion then needs a fully independent, human-irregular scheduler per fake: 1000 clones means 1000 separately-jittered sources, not one cron job, so duplication buys no cover.
